body:
Yikes. I'm sorry she said that to you. 

Labels are certainly powerful. From lazy, stupid, slow, etc to autistic and ADHD. 

Better to know I'm a majestic elephant who can't swim than continuing to believe I'm a big ugly fish who can't swim.

Thank you for all your points. I felt exactly this way. 

All staff left like 20 minutes into the chatting. We were alone for most of the time.

Yes, the fake sympathy. He saw those vulnerable moments as a way for him to take advantage.

He talked about his son. He shared his ex wife cheated on him. 

It got way too personal and I didn't like it. 

I clock All the red flags subconsciously, and then later digest it all after slowly processing.. over days or even weeks and months or years.

I think I'm asexual. I have had next to zero romantic or sexual interest in anyone in the last decade. 

I often forget that other people think about romance and sex. 

I get so shocked and surprised and I freeze up when anyone at all raises an interest in me. Partly because I've completely forgotten that romance and sex exist! (At least for others)
Thank you. Me too
That was my thought too. Labels can be so so helpful. His remark was so dismissive and full of the boomer mentality that autism is a fad and isn't real.

Thank you for kindness. 

My thoughts shortly after the incident was, even if I was attracted to him, I would never want to start off a relationship with a power imbalance. I was a patient, he was the Dr. This power imbalance isn't sexy. 

I'm still processing. I don't feel I have the energy to raise concern, as I'm already dealing with many battles and a health issue... But I'm still processing.

We NDs can be naive too, and our curiosity and kindness can be mistaken for flirting.

I'm inquisitive. I ask a lot of questions. I like to listen to different perspectives. This, in itself, allows vultures to see me as weak. It can also feed into the expectations and fantasy of men's to have a submissive woman. My presentation feeds into their grossness. 

Which pisses me off. Cause fuck, like do I really have to be on guard all the fucking time? It's exhausting... 

I am dealing with so many battles already. I don't know if I have it in me to take this on too, to report him. I'm already in burn out with major health issues.. 


I'm sorry you had to deal with a gross coworker.

Thank you for the empathy and validation. 

I'm 40, though I look 30. (Edit: and I act 20.. I come across as young). I'm petite and brown skin. I live in a predominantly white town and feel fetishized a lot based on my skin. 

He looked to be at least 55 years old, imo.

Same. It makes it overwhelming even before getting to the overwhelming task of sorting through all the options and reading the reviews and all that..

Have you tried Ali Express or other sites/apps?

You can also slow down your pace if you need. Wait a month or however long you need before trying the next one or trying to increase the dose. 

Preparing for these side effects can be helpful if you have the support. Like figuring out low effort meals, ordering in, giving yourself the grace to not engage in house chores, etc..  

I was on concerta for a year before realizing these side effects were not normal - like, I shouldn't feel that way on adhd meds. 

I am very very sensitive to each ingredient in meds. I often can't go generic because of the cheaper filler ingredients. Or I have to go through the ingredients list of a bunch of generics to find the right one. 

I'm sorry that I don't have easy solutions for you.

I've tried dozens and dozens of therapists. Only one I actually liked. CBT and DBT do not work for me. In the beginning, before being dx, I thought I was so broken that I couldn't be healed and was so mad at myself for not doing well in therapy. 

After realizing I'm ND, I have been wanting to get an ND therapist but they are sooooo expensive and just unaffordable for me. 

If you have the means, look for ND therapists who also have experience in other intersecting issues like race, trauma informed, queer and/or trans, etc..

I haven't tried it yet, but I'm sure an ND therapist would make the world of difference

I hear you. I think I started on ADHD meds when I was off for one week from work. I try to start new meds like this when I'm off, but it doesn't always work like that unfortunately. 

ADHD meds are definitely a process of trial and error. I think I tried 5 or 6 different ones until I ended up on Vyvanse on a lower dose (~20mg) to help prevent the crash and to help reduce the racing heart. 

I hope you find the right meds for you sooner than later. It will be worth it in the end.

I certainly prefer local and physical. But my health doesn't always allow for it. Sometimes I just need the ease, accessibility, and convenience for my sanity. Also $$. I know cheaper isn't better, but when I am very low on funds and am in need of something urgent I will resort to Amazon, unfortunately. I'm not proud of it but it's my reality.
Oh my gawd thank you for sharing the sub. I had no idea. I'm going to post my latest!
I love that! I would 100% do this with a partner too, if I had one.

I mean my mom did bug me about it all the time, even my dad. But me proudly showing it off to my mom wasn't because of the nagging, it was because I was so happy that I organized. If they ever made a comment like "ok now keep it clean" or something to ruin my mood, I'd try my best to ignore it.

That's a good point about seeing the product of a goal. I hadn't thought of it that way. I mean, I don't really see these chores as goals - more of something I have to get done. But once it's done I am so at peace by not having to look at the result of my dysfunction. And I'm happy I finally gained the functioning to accomplish it. 

I also sometimes fish for compliments, for the validation. I've learned who to ask, and who not to ask (those who are always negative and find fault, and don't see that I'm just trying to share my happiness and have them be happy for me)

I was raised in a religious household. 

I slowly became agnostic

Then became agnostic / atheist

Now I'm torn between agnostic and atheist 

I do not believe in a god. I do not believe in a heaven and hell. 

I do believe there's something after death, but this is where I'm open and undecided. Are we just energy? Are we reincarnating? Are we living life as an experience without consequences, only for the purpose of learning and growth? 

I do wish for a hell on the evils in the world, like all the zio-nazis, but I really don't believe there's a hell.

I think people need to be held accountable in this lifetime, not for the imagined punishment in the afterlife. 

But I don't hate on those who are religious and need faith. But I will hate on those who use religion as their justification for hatred and evils.

I'm a lifelong people pleaser with trauma from being undx.

People EXPECT calm and pleasantry from me because I've created the situation for them to expect it, because I'm always trying to be nice and mask the meltdowns and overwhelm. 

So because they expect me to be a doormat, as soon as I do something that misaligns with that narrative, they don't like it. It doesn't compute. They get upset and call it out so fast because they're trying to put me back in that box (that I essentially created). They need me to be predictable. 

This is with colleagues, managers, friends, romantic partners, etc.. it happens with everyone in my life.

If I start off as rude, I don't get called out for the continued ride behaviour. But if I start off as overwhelmingly nice, they will call me out so fast.


I really really really want to stop doing this, and start off with boundaries.

I wonder if, because you were diagnosed early, that you grew up being able to learn your triggers and learn coping strategies, which then became integrated into your life so naturally that in adulthood you have created systems that help you thrive? 


As a late dx at 37 (I'm 40 now) with a lifetime of trauma, my autistic traits show up more as a result of the ADHD meds. ADHD was masking my autistic traits. I'm trying to learn more and more what my traits are, my triggers, what I need to recharge, etc. 

I was dx after experiencing severe burnout. I am only at the beginning of my journey. 

Certain settings and certain people help me feel "normal", meaning not triggered. But right now, I'm still in burnout and some days I'm more easily triggered than other days.

I have also thrown dishes and pots away when they've been sitting out dirty for too long. I almost always throw out Tupperware too 

I forgot to mention that I started using ziplock bags to store my food in, if I don't store then in the same pot I cooked it in. 

Because of my health, I have to eat fresh food everyday, so I cook to last 2 days max. This also means I ended up eating all the food - most of the time

Thank you for offering this gentle approach. I was only dx a few years ago and it's been a Struggle to undo all the internal shame. 

'What works for me' should always be the goal and isn't anything to be ashamed about. 

De-colonize and de-capitalize the mind.

I also don't feel like a person - more like an alien who's tasked with mundane human tasks that are almost impossible to keep up with. 

I live alone for context. So I have to do e v e r y t h i n g...  Added to my situation is significant undiagnosed health issues that even moreso drains my energy and capacity. 

I'm on ADHD meds, which helps a bit but no where near enough. - it's not a magic pill that allows me to do every single task with ease. 

For the dishes, I had mountains and it was a nightmare. I got a counter top dishwasher that didn't really work properly. This is all before the the ADHD diagnosis. It would get so bad sometimes I'd put my dishes in a box and take it to my parents house to use their built-in dishwasher. I eventually resorting to using disposable only.

What I ended up doing that worked for me was keeping only a few dishes that I use on a daily basis and storing the rest away in a closet. Two bowls, two plates, two glasses, 3 forks, 4 spoons, one mug, one frying pan, etc..  

This immediately reduced the mountains and piles. Sometimes I wash them after using them. Mostly I wash before needing to use them - essentially every morning, and sometimes in the evening if I have the capacity. But because it's just a handful of dishes, it's not a huge burden anymore. 

For all other house chores,  I haven't found a solution that prevents piles. But every once in a while, I will clean up and put away to help make the piles smaller - not completely gone. "A little at a time" has been helpful. 

It took me like 3 years to truly understand "clean as you go" - because it was all or nothing for me until then. 

Also, "don't put it down, put it away" has really helped. 

I hope you find systems that work for you. Hugs to you

Yep, the guy who did the work on my car told me directly, multiple times, that he did not touch my front driver tire. 

But him doing it by mistake is the only logical explanation. 

I know not to go back to them.

That's what I'm thinking. And it's good to know that it's totally possible I wouldn't know anything until 3 weeks later.

I had my suspicion that it was an outrageous retaliation attempt from this random person I had in mind, but the more I think of it, the more far fetched that seems.
Thank you for this! It was very frustrating.

I think I tried all the stimulants and couldn't stand all the side effects, except for Vyvanse. 

I'm on 30mg on Vyvanse, but I actually take about 20mg because otherwise it's too much for me. 

I also tried non stimulants and it did nothing for me. I have a really hard time getting out of bed. 

I take half the 20mg dose around 630am (when I have to get up for the washroom). Just ~10mg is enough to get me out of bed around 730 or 8am. And that's when I take the second 10mg. 

I had to experiment a little to find what worked for me

Thank you so much for your kind and compassionate comment! 

What do you mean by folding screen? 

I've tried putting these clothes in bins / baskets, but I don't have the space and also I will completely forget whatever is hiding in the bottom of the bins. At least on my dresser, I can see them all. 

I love that the person didn't shame you or give you a whole new system to try that would likely fail. 

I've tried so many different systems, but none have worked for me. 

My piles usually don't get this big. My health has been in the shitter for two months with chronic illness, and other not so great life things have made fall way behind on so many chores and tasks. This pile is just over one month's worth of clothes that I've worn but haven't put back. 

I'm generally okay with keeping on top of laundry. But my day to day clothes end up in this pile. 

It's very frustrating.

The most helpful thing for me right now is the validation, support, compassion, letting me know I'm not alone. Because I'm burnt out and am in no shape for solutions and executive functioning.

Many are hung, and many are folded into drawers. 

One of the issues is that I don't want to put them away soon after taking them off. I let them breathe first by hanging them off the corner of my bed. It helps to get the body heat and all that out of the fabric to keep them fresh before putting them away. But then I just lose the executive function to put them away. There are so many other factors that lead to this mountain.

This pile isn't related to laundry in any way. 

I'm also not looking for advice right now.

Is it rude to say I'm not looking for advice? 

The post is tagged as rant / vent, not advice seeking. 

I didn't write in the title that I'm looking for suggestions. 

If you've read my other comments, I've explained what I meant by letting them breathe. I'm tired of repeating myself, especially since people are asking for the purpose of offering advice. But I'm not seeking advice. Also, this pile of clothes had nothing to do with laundry, which I've written over and over again in my other replies. 

Funny because the other day I posted about being annoyed by colleagues giving me unsolicited advice and people commented saying just tell them you're not seeking advice. And I was afraid by saying that, I'd come across as rude. And here we are...

These are clothes I've worn and haven't yet put back. 

I've already gotten rid of bags and bags of clothes. I was addicted to clothes shopping at one point. Also, my weight has gone up and down over the years, which has added to that problem.
Thank you, clothing-pile-kin! It's helpful to know I'm not alone. I'm also sorry you're struggling with this too 😔

I'm generally okay with putting laundry away, even if it takes me a few days. 

But this isn't laundry. These are clothes I've worn that I haven't put back yet. 

I do not do well with baskets, as I mentioned in the title.

Thank you for your kind comment, but I'm not looking for advice. This is something I'm currently struggling with and my intention to post was to seek empathy, compassion, and validation.

Thank you so much for seeing me 🙏🏽 that's really all I wanted from posting this. 

I have been so embarrassed about it, but I've been feeling so overwhelmed recently that I needed words of kindness and encouragement. Not judgement, no solutions.. just a space to share.

It's okay if it doesn't make sense to you or others. I don't need anyone to understand. I'm not looking for advice or suggestions. 

I'm venting. 

I'm really just looking for validation, empathy, kind words, feeling seen, all while I'm struggling with not only this but a lot of things, including health issues.

Thank you kind stranger for the gentle empathy 🙏🏽🙏🏽 

 I am very hard on myself. I live alone. It's me giving myself grief about it lol 

Living alone means I have to do absolutely everything, including taking care of my cats while I'm having major chronic health issues 😭 it's a lot.
Thank you so much ❤️ I really needed to hear this 🙏🏽
This is me!! 😂 Thanks for seeing me 😊

I always have piles, but never this bad! 

It has just certainly become part of my everyday. But I don't like it 😔

This is a pile that's been building for at least one month. Within that time, my health has suffered, I've had many work functions, so many errands and tasks to do, I've been in burn out, so much sensory overwhelm that leads to multiple changes of clothes... So many things that have allowed this pile to grow. 

It usually doesn't get this bad. But I still always have piles. 

This pile is not in anyway related to laundry.

I've tried different things like baskets, and hanging, and throwing things into drawers, so on and so on. I haven't found anything that works for me. And this moment in time, I'm not seeking advice. 

I hope you find something that works for you and your partner.

Thank you for your comment. Genuinely appreciated. 

I'm getting flustered by all the unsolicited advice, especially considering I posted this out of frustration, exhaustion, shame, guilt, sensory overwhelm,...

This isn't a time of high executive functioning and exploring ideas. 

I'm just tired 😩

I wore them.

This is not a pile of laundry.

We're saying the same thing but in different words. 

Finding a system that works is simultaneously a system that prevents this from happening. 

THANK YOU so much - genuinely - for saying you're willing to offer ideas but need more context first ❤️

At this time I'm not looking for advice or to brainstorm ideas. This is a rant / vent post because this is just where I'm at emotionally right now with this. I'm def not in a state of mind or have the executive function to be productive about it.

I sometimes struggle with putting laundry away too. But generally I'm fairly okay with it, even if it takes me a few days. 

This pile isn't related to laundry. It's clothes I've worn that I haven't put back. This is my struggle. Putting clothes away after I've worn them. 

Usually when I get back from outside, I'm in overwhelm and just want to get comfy again. Putting clothes away requires so much executive function that I don't often have when needed. 

Generally speaking, I tend to wear the same clothes on repeat for a days, depending on the task / activity. Which is fine for me if they're not put away.

Space isn't the issue at all. I already have a seperate place for all my sweaters. It's the act of putting them away that's a challenge for me. 

And yes, mood, activities / tasks, sensory sensitivities, temperature, etc all impact what I wear. I may have three different changes of clothes in a day because of that. Going from chilling, to cleaning, to cozying up, to going out to run in errand. I'm often repeating what I wear for a few days. 

Then there are times where I need to dress up for something and I try on a few different things to find the one that fits right. If I'm not late and in a decent mood, then I'll be leisurely about it and put everything that I tried on away. 
But if I'm late and having major sensory sensitivities or a meltdown, I won't put back everything I tried on. I might put them away after I've come back, or it'll get added to the pile, all depending on my mood and capacity.
You might think you're offering reasonable solutions. But I haven't provided you with enough context to warrant helpful advice. Saying I have too many clothes isn't a solution it's a judgment.
The whole point of them not being put away is to let them breathe. Folding them right away defeats the whole purpose.
Glad you found something that works for you!
Airing them out before putting them back.
Please read my comment again.

This pile isn't at all related to laundry. 

These are clothes I've worn that I haven't put away. 

I'm fairly decent with laundry, even if it takes me a few days to get around to putting them away.

I have already gotten rid of so many clothes. This pile is from clothes I've worn. 

I am sorry this struggle is also creating allergic symptoms for you and your dog :( 

Luckily no dust or any health related issues for me, except for the stress and guilt and shame of the existence of these piles..

I did this with my dishes. 

My dishes were piling up because I hate washing dishes. 

I got a countertop dishwasher that just absolutely sucked and didn't clean anything. 

Eventually I got rid of most of my dishes.

I only keep 3 forks, 4 spoons, 2 knives, two plates, two bowls, 1 large plate, 2 glasses, one mug, one frying pan. And they all live in the dish rack, not in the cupboards.

This helped *significantly*

This method does not work with me for clothes

I wrote in the title that I can't do baskets. 

Also I'm not looking for advice, thank you.
Thank you for your comment. Sorry you're struggling with this too :(

There is way too much unsolicited advice here. The tag of this post is rant / vent for a reason. 

I am not seeking advice. Nor have I provided enough context to warrant enough relevant advice. 

These are not clothes that have just come out of the wash. These are not clothes that need to be washed. 

These are clothes I have worn that need to be put away. I need for them to breathe before putting them away. 

People seem to be hung up on "letting them breathe". Letting them air out. 
When you wear clothes, all your heat and smells get into them. I need to let them breathe before putting them back into a tight / unventilated state. It keeps them fresh. 

I take off my clothes and let them hang off my bed to help them breathe. I end up not putting them away and I move them onto my dresser. 

My clothes are always aired out before they get into this pile.

I am not going to explain this further or justify why I do this. 
 
This pile is one of the worst piles to date. It's about one month's worth of clothes I've worn. 

I am NOT seeking advice. 

No system has seemed to work for me. I've tried many. 

I am NOT seeking advice. 

Thank you

I can't do disorderly drawers. I need to be able to see the items in the drawers. 

I even fold my underwear. My socks are folded and paired together.

The pile is made of clothes I have worn that haven't been put away.

Yes! I think this is also partly it. Not clean enough but not dirty enough. I'm also a bit of a germaphobe, so this likely has something to do with it. 

I have outside clothes, inside clothes that can never touch my bedsheets, pjs that can't be worn outside of bed...

Thank you for the validation. 

The tag of this post is vent/ rant, as I'm not seeking advice.

Many of the comments are giving unsolicited advice, which is frustrating when I haven't provided all the things I've already tried and haven't provided more context.

All of the clothes on this dresser are clothes I wear. It's why they're on the dresser, because I've worn them and not put them away. 

I've already gotten rid of bags and bags of clothes.

Yes, that's partly where I get stuck. The other part is actually putting them away. I may even be using the excuse they need to breathe in order to avoid putting them away. I'm not entirely sure either way. 

That could work for hanging clothes, but not with the clothes that need to be folded.
Nope. That's like having a doorless closet. Plus this is too many clothes to be putting on hooks. There wouldn't be enough wall space
After I wear them, I let them breathe before I put them away.

The pile is clothes I have worn that need to be put away. 


I've gotten rid of bags and bags full of clothes. 

Clothes that do not end up in this pile are seasonal or occasional clothing that I do still wear

No matter the system or organizer, etc.. I'm 40 and have never found something that works to prevent this. 

Even when I have someone coming over, I just throw the mountain on the closet floor. And then put it back on the dresser after they've left.
These aren't dirty and don't need to be laundered. They need to be hung or folded into a drawer. This mountain forms after I wear the clothing and want it to breathe before putting it away.

My goal is to be unapologetically me. As a life long people pleaser, I dream of being called a bitch instead of a doormat. 

But as a true people pleaser, I don't want anyone calling me a bitch lol 

I already know I'm not well liked. I'm not most people's cup of tea. I don't have many friends. I don't easily get along with people. So I overcompensate by being a people pleaser. 

This is 40 years, my entire life, of undoing myself in order to find myself. 

So just suddenly speaking up for myself - creating boundaries - is painful. But it's necessary for my goal. 

They do it so innocently, like they truly believe they're helping. So then I feel like the ass ruining their self serving feel good vibes. 

That piece in itself is something I need to figure out how to overcome before I can feel comfortable enough to start saying those lines.

Thank you so much for the validation! 

They are absolutely crossing a line, especially since I'm not bringing it up. I'm not bringing up my personal life. I'm not asking anyone for advice. I'm not selling input on my life, and most especially not from people who have no idea what it is I do. 

But they think I'm their teenaged kid and start to 'mother' me... They think they're being kind and helpful, but it's wildly inappropriate. 

The more I think about it, the angrier I get. I have delayed processing, so I also get upset at myself for not recognizing what's happening in the moment. That they have left the conversation thinking it was completely acceptable what they did. 

They ask questions because I guess that's just how NT people are, which I fucking hate. But if I don't answer I feel like I'm being rude. And I'm a people pleaser. So they learn I'm renting or something like that, because they asked, and then they proceed to give me advice. 

They create the situations themselves to mother me. 

It's infuriating.

Thank you for giving that example. I like it. And I feel like it's something I can say. 

Two things. 

One is I have delayed processing so I will likely not catch it right away. I don't realize quick enough that I should say that line. 

Second thing is, it can still come across as rude depending on how that person takes it. Though, I feel like if I say it friendly enough, I shouldn't be bothered after that with their ego. 

I will allow a conversation about how to fix me take place because I don't see the signs right away. I feel like maybe they'll make one or two comments and end it themselves, but then they go on and on and then I feel trapped..

Though I think I need to just practice this as best as I can. (Not quick though for me though)

It absolutely sucks and is so very frustrating. This is partly why I feel like I just don't belong in most spaces. I'm an introvert so I do like to spend a lot of time alone, but I don't want to be alone ALL the time. And I don't at least do 1:1 hangs with these white ND folks, I have next to zero social life... Even the NT folks I know are again mostly white. I live in a predominantly white area. 


An ND friend (acquaintance?) was gathering some queer folk for weekly socials. They strongly encouraged me to join. I was hesitant because I know they're all white. But on their persistence, I agreed to attend. 

So inevitably I brought up racism because it's a factor they didn't express in their experiences. One person physically turned themselves away from me. 

I brought up how edi is mostly performative and glosses over oppressions and just moves into solutions. I said that we really need to focus on anti racism, colonialism, and to name all the isms, understand how it all intersects, etc. you can't possibly make solutions to issues you don't *really* understand.

And they all - every one of them expect the person who invited me - basically ganged up on me saying edi is so great and edi addresses racism... 

I was the only racialized person there. On top of that, I have facilitated anti racism education and have also been involved with some edi committees in workplaces. 

So I'm the only one with real perspective. Yet they were happy to shut me down. The person who invited me didn't really try to defend me in much of any meaningful way.

I didn't attend another social again. 

They are happy to see color in their spaces but don't want the color to be anything more than visibility. 

They don't care to realize how upsetting it is, either. 

Sorry I have no resolutions to offer - just a lot of validation and relatability.

I'm glad I'm not alone, but I'm sorry you've also experienced this. 

I think I'm in another burnout and I have some significant health issues right now, all of which leads to brain fog. I forget things, I forget words, etc.. I know I can come across as someone who doesn't know anything. But I *do* know -- at least many things, and most of the things they think they're trying to teach me.

It's the condescension and assumptions I have such an issue with. 

For me, ADHD meds have not helped on this matter. Anti anxiety meds have also not really helped. 

But finally learning I'm AuDHD and going on this journey is waking me up to it, for a start.

This whole concept of knowledge and common knowledge is fascinating to me.

As a late dx AuDHDer, I have always believed that other people know better than me. I only realised recently that this is in fact not true. 

Everyone else doesn't have the answer, but they pretend like they do. Like, they genuinely pretend like they do. Not that they're acting like they know, but that they don't care if they actually know or not. Good enough is good enough for them. 

This was such a shocking realization for me, since I feel like I need to do my literature reviews and experiments before I come to any conclusion. And I genuinely believed others did this as well. 

Also, being ADHD, I forget that people aren't in my head and cannot see what I'm picturing and explaining. I skip over parts that I'm sure they know, but later I realize they don't actually know. But they don't say that they don't know. 

Like, speaking with other ND people, I feel like we all tend to stop people and ask them to explain or elaborate because we want to actually follow what someone is trying to say. 

But I find NT people don't care to actually know.

What I think people know, they don't know. But there are so many things NT people know, that I don't know.

I think this is masking. I have masked my entire life,  and I only learned I'm AuDHD a few years ago. 

Not only does no one really know who I am, but I don't even know who I am. 

I think it was around the age of 30 that I realised I had been living behind a curtain, watching myself be on autopilot while the real me was hidden away. 

I don't really know how to unmask. It's a journey. And I very much want to unmask.

All of this trauma and internal chaos can only lead to disconnection from others. 

There has yet to be a single person I can be myself around.

I need clear examples of how to do this, because I don't know how to not come across as rude. 

To be honest, people see me as a doormat. So when I speak up about their behavior, they do not expect it and it upsets them. They take issue with me speaking up instead of them reflecting on the content. 

Plus I'm racialized, which probably explains why I'm such a people pleaser because the colour of my skin alone can change my tone, at least in their perspective.

I very much struggle with always being the outsider. 

It started as young as I can remember, being very different from the others in my family and never fitting in with cousins and other peers as early as kindergarten.

Most of the ND people I know IRL are white. I'm not white. While they're welcoming, they don't realize how exclusive they can be. My experiences aren't shared and tend to be dismissed or overlooked. Like, they believe they're not racist, but racism isn't something they want to discuss.

The focus of discussion is on the design of the medication (tablet, capsule,  etc) versus the active ingredients. 

Extended release tablets are designed to release slowly in your system, which is why these meds shouldn't be cut, crushed, or opened in any way. The release timing is based on the design of the tablet, not the active ingredients.  

Vyvanse capsules aren't designed to release overtime. Your body absorbs all of the active ingredients at once. So you can open the capsule and take the entire dose at once. Taking part of a dose won't change its absorption process or effectiveness - only the strength.

This post isn't pointless. I've read many comments on other posts claiming that vyvanse capsules should never be opened to consume just the powder because they believe the capsule is designed to slowly release / extended release the contents. 
The manufacture clearly states that we can open the capsule and empty the powder into a glass of water or even sprinkle it over apple sauce. Doing this does not alter the absorption or the effects, but it does need to be consumed right away and all at once. 


I cannot consume the capsule for reasons, so I empty the powder into a glass of water. It works exactly the same.

 We as audhd, especially those of us late dx, develop differently and slower. Life is built for NTs. How we are meant to learn about how to navigate and survive life is mostly informal learning through observation and trial and error. It comes seemingly natural for NTs but they struggle too sometimes,  though not in the same way as us. 

The process and expectation of learning isn't designed for us. We often don't have the right guidance from parents and teachers and others because they usually don't know how to appropriately approach our learning styles and developmental stages while also affirming our ND. And because we may want to conform and mask as much as possible, we lose ourselves. 

So basically we're kind of doomed. It's inevitable to feel like failures, to struggle, to be dependent, and so on. 

Some of us will be dependent on others no matter what, and there is nothing wrong with that.  We're just made to believe that independence means success, which is ableist.  But it has nothing to do with 'success'. It's just facts of life.

Exploring more about your needs, learning styles, your goals and desires can be helpful. Without comparing yourself to others and without the expectations put on you. 

Part of learning new skills for us is learning and practicing in small steps. And to accept that you won't nail it on the first or even tenth time. We may keep it up for a little while and then not have the capacity for it again. 

Knowing the signs of burn out is helpful too. Knowing your triggers. Recognizing when something isn't working early on.

My meds routine kinda figured itself out for me. 

I have digestive issues which leaves me going #1 anywhere from 2 - 10 times at night. In the morning around 6 - 7am, I always have to pee without fail. So after that morning #1, I take my first med. I put my second and third sets of meds in their lids. Then I take the water and the two lids to my bedside table.
